concepts.name: Human Wants
concepts.description: Human wants are desires for goods and services that provide satisfaction. They are unlimited, recurring, and vary according to time, place, income, and individual preferences.
concepts.learning_outcome: Students will be able to explain the characteristics of human wants and distinguish between different types of wants.

concepts.name: Economic Resources
concepts.description: Economic resources are the inputs used to produce goods and services. Since these resources are limited, they must be utilized efficiently.
concepts.learning_outcome: Students will be able to identify various economic resources and explain their role in production.

concepts.name: Scarcity
concepts.description: Scarcity arises because available resources are insufficient to satisfy unlimited human wants, making choice an unavoidable part of economic activity.
concepts.learning_outcome: Students will be able to explain how scarcity creates the need for economic decision-making.

concepts.name: Goods
concepts.description: Goods are tangible products that satisfy human wants. They may be classified as free goods, economic goods, consumer goods, or capital goods.
concepts.learning_outcome: Students will be able to classify goods into different categories with suitable examples.

concepts.name: Services
concepts.description: Services are intangible activities provided to satisfy human needs, such as education, healthcare, banking, and transportation.
concepts.learning_outcome: Students will be able to distinguish between goods and services using real-life examples.

concepts.name: Utility
concepts.description: Utility refers to the ability of a good or service to satisfy a human want. It depends on the needs and preferences of consumers.
concepts.learning_outcome: Students will be able to explain the concept of utility and its importance in consumption.

concepts.name: Land
concepts.description: Land includes all natural resources used in production, such as soil, forests, minerals, and water resources.
concepts.learning_outcome: Students will be able to identify land as a factor of production and explain its characteristics.

concepts.name: Labour, Capital and Enterprise
concepts.description: Labour provides human effort, capital includes man-made productive assets, and enterprise organizes other factors while bearing business risk.
concepts.learning_outcome: Students will be able to explain the roles of labour, capital, and enterprise in production.

concepts.name: Factor Rewards
concepts.description: Each factor of production receives a specific reward: rent for land, wages for labour, interest for capital, and profit for enterprise.
concepts.learning_outcome: Students will be able to match each factor of production with its corresponding reward.

concepts.name: Economic Activities
concepts.description: Economic activities involve the production, exchange, distribution, and consumption of goods and services to satisfy human wants.
concepts.learning_outcome: Students will be able to identify different types of economic activities in everyday life.

concepts.name: Economic Systems
concepts.description: Different countries organize their economies through capitalist, socialist, or mixed economic systems, each having distinct ownership and decision-making structures.
concepts.learning_outcome: Students will be able to compare the main features of capitalist, socialist, and mixed economies.

concepts.name: Economic Agents
concepts.description: Households, firms, and governments are the primary economic agents responsible for production, consumption, regulation, and distribution.
concepts.learning_outcome: Students will be able to explain the roles of major economic agents in an economy.

concepts.name: Understanding Basic Economic Terminology
concepts.description: This chapter introduces the foundational concepts of economics, including wants, resources, goods, services, utility, factors of production, and economic systems.
concepts.learning_outcome: Students will be able to apply fundamental economic terminology correctly while explaining basic economic situations.
